research_question: In the existing historical ObjectNav full-200 evaluation, is lower policy-independent target physical size associated with lower success after first establishing category-level sample size/uncertainty and accounting for available pre-policy task difficulty covariates?
hypothesis: H-SIZE: smaller targets, measured from target-object 3D bounding-box metadata independent of policy behavior, have lower navigation success.
competing_explanations: H-CATEGORY: semantic category rather than physical size explains low SR
H-DIFFICULTY: house/task difficulty, expert path length, or initial distance explains the pattern
H-SAMPLE: apparent ~50% category SR is unstable because per-category n is small
H-BEHAVIOR: low visible-pixel counts are consequences of failed search/approach rather than an exogenous target-size cause
unique_variable: Primary explanatory variable is per-task median 3D bounding-box volume across all valid broad-synset target object IDs; median maximum side length is a robustness descriptor.
control: Continuous analysis first; large-target tertile is descriptive control after tertiles are defined on the full analyzable set without success labels.
fixed_conditions: 0 GPU, 0 episodes, no model load, no AI2-THOR
Use existing historical full-200 raw results, task specs, and static scene metadata only
Do not define physical size using distance or trajectory-derived visible pixels
Treat historical AUC 0.955/0.982/0.992 as exploratory stop-legality Probe evidence, not small-target evidence
metrics: Per-category n, successes, SR, Wilson 95% CI
Continuous effect estimate for log physical size versus success with uncertainty
If complete data permit: logistic(success ~ log_size + expert_length [+ independently available initial_distance])
Small/medium/large tertile SR with Wilson 95% CI
Missing size metadata count and analyzable n
Duplicate stable-task-key check and reconciliation with historical 200 tasks / 173 successes
Optional downstream failure morphology from already-recorded visible pixels / termination type, explicitly non-causal
expected_result: Either establish that the reported low-SR categories are statistically credible and that policy-independent target size is associated with failure, or weaken the size narrative in favor of category/difficulty/sample explanations.
falsifying_result: Low-SR categories are unstable under uncertainty, physical size shows little/reversed association, or the association disappears under available difficulty controls.
stop_conditions: Any new model/simulator/GPU/episode execution would be required
Historical full-200 raw evidence cannot be reconciled with the 173/200 report
Stable task identity cannot be reconstructed
Physical-size metadata cannot be obtained statically
Size would have to be defined by distance or outcome-derived visible pixels
Any baseline/runtime code change is required
